methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective case-control biomarker study with 71 EC patients and 62 matched healthy controls, with matching for age, BMI, and smoking status. RT-qPCR methods are described in detail (kits, catalog numbers, thermocycling conditions) and gene-expression normalization to GAPDH (for HOTAIR) and U6 (for miR-646) follows common practice, though authors acknowledge these references may vary in circulation. Weaknesses include single-center design, modest sample size, only 15.5% advanced-stage patients limiting stage-based subgroup power, and no independent validation cohort. No power calculation is described and multiple univariate comparisons are performed without explicit multiplicity correction.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual case-control diagnostic biomarker study (Oxford 3b). The clinical question (non-invasive serum biomarker for EC diagnosis and staging) is relevant, but the reported diagnostic performance is modest (HOTAIR AUC 0.617, sensitivity 63.3%, specificity 61.2%), which the authors correctly note falls below clinically accepted thresholds. miR-646 distinguished advanced from early-stage disease with modest accuracy. The findings are hypothesis-generating with unclear near-term clinical utility.

reporting_quality.justification: As a diagnostic accuracy study, STARD is the applicable standard. The paper reports inclusion/exclusion criteria, reference standard (histopathology), index test procedures, ROC-derived cut-offs with sensitivity/specificity, and a brief limitations section. Gaps relative to STARD include no explicit flow diagram of participants, no blinding description for index vs reference tests, no indeterminate/missing data reporting, and no confidence intervals for AUC. Data-sharing statement and raw Cq values are not provided; primers are proprietary Qiagen assays.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors assert that, to their knowledge, serum (rather than tissue) HOTAIR and miR-646 levels have not been previously reported in clinical EC samples; prior evidence (Zhou et al. 2018, ref 33) established the HOTAIR/miR-646/NPM1 axis in EC cell lines and tissues. Extending this to serum is a meaningful but incremental translational step. The concept of HOTAIR as an EC tissue biomarker is well established in cited literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable with standard structure and a thorough introduction situating ncRNAs in EC. Figures and tables are referenced logically. However, the discussion is long and contains repetitive background on lncRNAs/miRs across non-EC cancers that dilute the focus, and some sentences are overlong. The interpretation of modest AUC values is appropriately cautious.

key_strengths: Age/BMI/smoking-matched case-control design with prospectively collected serum samples
RT-qPCR protocols and kits fully specified with catalog numbers
Author interpretation of modest AUCs is appropriately cautious and acknowledges clinical inadequacy
Novel focus on serum rather than tissue HOTAIR/miR-646 in EC
key_concerns: Diagnostic accuracy is below clinical thresholds (HOTAIR AUC 0.617; sensitivity/specificity 63.3/61.2%)
No independent validation cohort; single-center, relatively small sample
Only 15.5% of cases were advanced-stage, limiting power for stage-related analyses
Use of GAPDH/U6 as serum normalizers is debatable; no spike-in control used
STARD reporting incomplete (no participant flow diagram, blinding, AUC CIs not reported)
chief_reviewer.rationale: An incremental serum biomarker study with honest reporting but modest diagnostic performance and limited sample size; best fit is a lower-tier specialty oncology journal after major revisions addressing validation and STARD adherence.
